report_name: UK Police National Legal Database (PNLD) Breach Exposes Officer Data

threat_actors.name: Unknown Actor
threat_actors.description: The unidentified threat actor responsible for gaining unauthorized access to the Police National Legal Database (PNLD), exfiltrating sensitive contact information, and publishing it on a dark web forum.
threat_actors.goals: Data theft and public exposure of sensitive information related to UK law enforcement.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor likely exploited a misconfiguration or vulnerability in a public-facing Microsoft Power Apps application used by the PNLD to gain unauthorized access to the database.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exfiltrated a database containing sensitive contact information from the PNLD, which is hosted on the Microsoft Power Platform, a cloud environment.

vulnerabilities.name: Power Platform Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.description: A potential misconfiguration in the Microsoft Power Platform application used by the PNLD, such as improper table permissions, likely allowed unauthorized public access to the underlying database, leading to data exfiltration.

identities.name: Police National Legal Database (PNLD)
identities.description: A UK national legal information service supporting all 43 Home Office police forces, which was the primary victim of the data breach.

identities.name: UK Police Officers and Staff
identities.description: A class of individuals whose names, work email addresses, and organizational affiliations were exposed in the PNLD breach.

identities.name: UK Government and Justice Partners
identities.description: A class of individuals from government and criminal justice agencies whose contact details were exposed in the PNLD breach.

identities.name: Ask the Police Service Users
identities.description: Members of the public who used the 'Ask the Police' service and had their names and email addresses exposed in the breach.

identities.name: National Crime Agency (NCA)
identities.description: The UK agency responsible for investigating the PNLD data breach.

identities.name: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
identities.description: The UK's data protection regulator, which was notified of the PNLD breach.

infrastructure.name: Dark Web Forum
infrastructure.description: A forum on the dark web where the threat actor published the database stolen from the Police National Legal Database (PNLD).

indicators.name: Suspicious Email Targeting UK Law Enforcement
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Email Targeting UK Law Enforcement Post-PNLD Breach
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects suspicious emails targeting UK law enforcement personnel that may leverage information from the PNLD breach.
  This rule looks for emails with subjects referencing internal police matters or using specific ranks, sent to .police.uk or other government domains, which could indicate a targeted spear-phishing attempt.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/pnld-breach-exposes-uk-police-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  selection_keywords:
    Subject|contains:
      - 'Internal Memo'
      - 'Urgent Update'
      - 'Security Alert'
      - 'Case File'
      - 'Chief Constable'
      - 'Superintendent'
      - 'Inspector'
  selection_recipient:
    Recipient|endswith:
      - '.police.uk'
      - '.pnn.police.uk'
      - '.gov.uk'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects suspicious emails targeting UK law enforcement personnel that may leverage information from the PNLD breach, such as specific names and ranks, to increase legitimacy.

indicators.name: Anomalous Microsoft Power Platform Data Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Microsoft Power Platform Data Access
id: a2b3c4d5-e6f7-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects anomalous data access patterns in Microsoft Power Platform or Dataverse audit logs, which could indicate a misconfiguration being exploited, similar to the potential vector in the PNLD breach. This rule looks for data read operations by an anonymous or external user.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/pnld-breach-exposes-uk-police-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1530
  - attack.t1190
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: powerplatform
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'RetrieveMultiple'
    UserId|contains:
      - 'public'
      - 'anonymous'
      - '#EXT#'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects anomalous data access patterns in Microsoft Power Platform or Dataverse audit logs, which could indicate a misconfiguration being exploited, similar to the PNLD breach.

indicators.name: Anomalous Network Connection to Power Apps Content Domain
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Network Connection to Power Apps Content Domain
id: b3c4d5e6-f7a8-4c9d-0e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects anomalous network connections to content.powerapps.com from unusual sources or outside of expected business patterns, which could indicate reconnaissance or exploitation of a Power Apps portal. This rule flags non-browser user agents.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/pnld-breach-exposes-uk-police-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-03
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: low
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host: 'content.powerapps.com'
  filter:
    c-useragent|startswith:
      - 'Mozilla/'
      - 'Chrome/'
      - 'Safari/'
      - 'Edge/'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects anomalous network connections to content.powerapps.com from unusual sources or outside of expected business patterns, which could indicate reconnaissance or exploitation of a Power Apps portal.
